candidates.topic: Trees communicate underground via fungal networks
candidates.teaser: Forests have a secret internet — and trees have been using it for millions of years.
candidates.video_title: Trees Can Talk to Each Other Underground 🌲
candidates.video_description: Forests aren't just collections of individual trees — they're connected by a massive underground fungal network. Trees use this network to share nutrients and even warn each other about danger.
candidates.script: What if I told you that every forest on Earth has its own secret internet? Trees are connected underground through massive fungal networks called mycorrhizae. Through these threads, a mother tree can send sugar and nutrients directly to its struggling seedlings nearby. Even more shocking — when a tree is attacked by insects, it sends chemical warning signals through this network so neighboring trees can boost their own defenses. Scientists call it the Wood Wide Web. Trees aren't just standing there silently — they're constantly talking. So next time you walk through a forest, what do you think they're saying about you?

candidates.topic: A day on Venus is longer than its year
candidates.teaser: There's a planet where your birthday comes before your day even ends — and it's real.
candidates.video_title: On Venus, a Day Is Longer Than a Year 🪐
candidates.video_description: Venus spins so slowly on its axis that one full rotation takes longer than its entire orbit around the Sun. It also spins backwards compared to most planets.
candidates.script: Here's something that will break your brain — on Venus, a single day is actually longer than an entire year. Venus takes only 225 Earth days to orbit the Sun, but it spins so incredibly slowly on its own axis that one full rotation takes 243 Earth days. That means the year ends before the day does. And here's the twist — Venus also spins backwards compared to almost every other planet. If you stood on Venus, the Sun would rise in the west and set in the east. Scientists still don't fully agree on why Venus rotates this way. What do you think caused it?

candidates.teaser: You might have more in common with your morning smoothie than you ever wanted to know.
candidates.video_title: You Share 60% of Your DNA With a Banana 🍌
candidates.video_description: It sounds absurd, but humans and bananas share roughly 60% of the same genes. This reveals just how universal the building blocks of life really are.
candidates.script: You and a banana share about 60% of the same DNA. That's not a joke — it's genetics. Every living thing on Earth uses the same basic molecular machinery to survive: growing, repairing cells, converting food into energy. Those core processes are written in genes that have barely changed across hundreds of millions of years of evolution. We share around 85% of our DNA with mice, and about 99% with chimpanzees. But the banana fact is the one that really stops people cold. Think about it — the next time you peel a banana, you're holding something that's more than half genetically similar to you. So what does that make us, really?

candidates.topic: Cleopatra's needle obelisk and its hidden time capsule
candidates.teaser: One of the world's most famous ancient monuments is hiding a secret inside — and almost nobody knows about it.
candidates.video_title: There's a Time Capsule Hidden Inside an Ancient Obelisk
candidates.video_description: The Cleopatra's Needle obelisk in New York City contains a Victorian time capsule sealed inside its base in 1880. It holds newspapers, coins, a Bible, and even a photo of notable women of the era.
candidates.script: There's a 3,500-year-old Egyptian obelisk standing right in New York City's Central Park — and almost no one knows what's hidden inside its base. When the monument was installed in 1880, a group of Freemasons secretly sealed a time capsule beneath it. Inside: copies of the US Constitution, a map of New York, census records, coins, a Bible, and remarkably, photographs of notable American women of the time. The obelisk itself was carved under Pharaoh Thutmose the Third — it's older than Cleopatra by over a thousand years. Millions of people walk past it every year without a second glance. If you could add one thing to a time capsule today, what would it be?

candidates.topic: Crows hold grudges and recognize human faces
candidates.teaser: A crow you wronged years ago will remember your face — and it might tell its friends.
candidates.video_title: Crows Never Forget a Face — And They Hold Grudges 🐦
candidates.video_description: Crows can recognize individual human faces and remember people who have threatened them for years. They've even been observed teaching other crows to distrust specific humans.
candidates.script: If you ever make a crow angry, be very careful — because it will remember your face for years. Scientists at the University of Washington proved this by wearing specific masks while trapping crows. Afterward, the crows would dive-bomb and scold anyone wearing that exact mask — even years later, even researchers who had never personally bothered them. The crows had taught each other to recognize the threatening face. They can also recognize when someone is being kind, and will sometimes bring small gifts to people who feed them regularly. A bird with a brain the size of a walnut is capable of a social intelligence that most animals never develop. So — have you ever had a run-in with a crow?
